plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrubby plant with large, vividly colored bracts surrounding small yellow true flowers. In its native habitat it grows as a tall shrub, and it blooms as short winter days trigger color change.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; widely cultivated worldwide, outdoors in warm climates such as southern California, Florida, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts, not petals. The plant needs about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness nightly for roughly 8 weeks to color up.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and is popular in southern gardens for autumn and early winter color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to produce a useful culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with a umbrella-shaped canopy and fern-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere's early summer it is covered with large, brilliant flowers, and long woody seed pods follow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); also blooms May to July in the Northern Hemisphere tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Brazil, Australia, South Africa, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: In the wild in Madagascar the species is endangered, even though it is among the most widely planted ornamental trees in the tropics.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low, evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped flowers that open in the cold of winter. It thrives in woodland and shady garden borders and tolerates frost and snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid winter (December to February)
plants.location: Native to the mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its common name it is not a true rose; all parts are toxic, and old folklore tied its winter blooming to the Christmas season.
